case_name: Hey Listen Mandyhan, L.L.C. v. Trody

issues.label: Meaning of 'dwelling' under R.C. 5313.01(B)
issues.why: Whether the existing garage-turned-apartment qualifies as a dwelling determines if Chapter 5313 applies at all.

issues.label: Whether dwelling must be newly erected
issues.why: The trial court held a preexisting structure cannot count, requiring interpretation of 'improved by virtue of a dwelling having been erected.'

issues.label: Relevance of commercial zoning to dwelling status
issues.why: Trody objected that zoning improperly precluded finding a residential dwelling, so its legal relevance must be resolved.

issues.label: Actual residential use versus original commercial purpose
issues.why: Whether the structure's original non-residential purpose or its current residential use controls the dwelling determination.

issues.label: Whether the two agreements form a land installment contract
issues.why: Contemporaneous lease and purchase agreement may together constitute a R.C. 5313.02 contract despite separate titles.

issues.label: Effect of the lease's integration clause
issues.why: The court relied on integration to exclude the purchase agreement, raising whether parol/companion agreements can be considered.

issues.label: Simultaneously executed documents construed together
issues.why: Ohio law generally reads contemporaneous instruments on the same transaction as one agreement, potentially overriding integration.

issues.label: Contract ambiguity and parties' intent
issues.why: The magistrate found ambiguity requiring extrinsic evidence to determine lease-versus-installment-contract intent.

issues.label: Substantial compliance with R.C. 5313.02
issues.why: Trody argued substantial compliance saves the contract even if formal requirements are unmet; court found it moot.

issues.label: Whether ten-day cure notice was required
issues.why: R.C. 5313.06 mandates a ten-day notice to cure, which was not given, if a land installment contract exists.

issues.label: Twenty-percent payment triggering foreclosure
issues.why: Under R.C. 5313.07, over 20% paid requires foreclosure rather than forcible entry and detainer.

issues.label: Adequacy of the three-day notice
issues.why: Whether a three-day FED notice suffices depends on which statutory regime governs the tenancy/vendee relationship.

issues.label: Refused tender of arrearage payments
issues.why: Trody attempted to cure after notice and Mandyhan refused, affecting the propriety of eviction.

issues.label: Characterization as option to purchase
issues.why: Whether the purchase agreement is a mere option contingent on lease completion rather than an installment sale.

issues.label: Allocation of extra payments to taxes/insurance
issues.why: Trody paid $570 rather than $459.10 rent, bearing on whether payments reflect a purchase arrangement.

issues.label: Credibility determinations on land-contract intent
issues.why: The court deferred to the magistrate crediting Mandyhan's witness, raising review of factual findings.

issues.label: Standard of review of magistrate's decision
issues.why: The trial court's review of objections and appellate review standards govern the analysis.

issues.label: Ruling on judicial notice requests
issues.why: The court never explicitly ruled on Trody's ledger judicial-notice requests, potentially affecting the record.

issues.label: Whether payment ledger totals were established
issues.why: Marie could not compute totals and remaining balance, affecting proof of the 20% threshold.

issues.label: Jurisdiction/propriety of FED under Chapter 1923
issues.why: If a land installment contract exists, FED may be improper and foreclosure required.

issues.label: Improvements made with seller's approval
issues.why: Trody's renovations with Grabow's materials may evidence intent for residential ownership relevant to the contract's nature.

issues.label: Landlord acquiescence to residential occupancy
issues.why: Mandyhan's non-objection to Trody residing may bear on the property's dwelling characterization and estoppel.
